concepts.def: How quickly reactants are used up or products form
Particles must collide with enough energy
Minimum energy for a successful collision
Speeds up rate without being used up
Forward and reverse rates equal in closed system

walkthroughs.body_html:
Four factors: concentration, temperature, surface area and catalyst.

More particles or more energy = more successful collisions per second.

Catalysts provide a lower activation energy pathway.

They are not used up in the reaction.

Enzymes are biological catalysts.

Some reactions reach an equilibrium: forward rate = reverse rate.

Example: N2 + 3H2 to 2NH3 (Haber process).

Concentrations stay constant but reactions continue - dynamic equilibrium.
